newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index braced for record high.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index braced for record high.

text.p: Hong Kong shares are expected to push into record ground on Thursday, propelled by the Dow industrials' move to all-time highs overnight and continued strength in HSBC Holdings shares, brokers said.

"The Dow industrials closed above the 8,000 mark, Hong Kong stocks in London were up overnight and HSBC was strong, so the Hang Seng should test a new high today," said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Asia Securities.
The Dow industrials rose 63.17 points, or 0.79 percent, to a record closing high of 8,038.88. The Hang Seng Index hit an all-time intra-day high of 15,635.52 on Wednesday.
The blue-chip index closed 41.22 points, or 0.27 percent, lower at 15,446.02. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index surged 145.66 points, or 0.94 perecnt, to 15,591.68.
Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, said he saw upward movement on Thursday, although poor sentiment on properties could introduce some weakness.

Government forecasts on Wednesday suggesting a dramatic increase in the supply of flats in coming years might affect earnings of property developers, To said, but there were indications no further measures would be needed unless there were renewed signs of speculation in the property market.
